contracts/chat_parts.py:R5:_audit_conten: R5 `isinstance(content, str)` in `_audit_content`. R5 `isinstance(part, TextPart)` in `_wire_content`'s parts loop. Nominal dispatch on the closed owned union: TextPart takes the `{'type': 'text'}` arm and the else arm is ImagePart, which is the only place in ELSPETH permitted to base64-encode image bytes onto the wire. Replacing this with polymorphism (a `wire_view()` on each part class) was considered and rejected: it would create a second exit for image bytes, which this module's docstring forbids - `wire_messages` and `audit_messages` are the only sanctioned exits. The union is guaranteed two-armed by `ChatMessage.__post_init__`, so the else arm needs no re-check.
contracts/chat_parts.py:R5:parts_hash:bo: R5 `isinstance(part, TextPart)` in `parts_hash`. This arm cannot be merged with `_audit_content`'s - that one emits `{'type','text'}` and this one emits `{'type','sha256'}` - which is why the dispatch is repeated rather than factored into a shared helper. contracts/sink_effects.py:R5:_contains_r: R5 `isinstance(value, RestrictedAuditExportSnapshotReader)` - the positive-detection arm of `_contains_restricted_reader`. This is a security control, not a shape check: RestrictedAuditExportSnapshotReader is a concrete class this module owns whose entire purpose is to be unserializable (`__deepcopy__` and `__reduce__` both raise), and this walk is what stops one being smuggled inside a sink plugin's evidence payload, where it would be frozen into the durable record and hand a later reader unscoped access to audit-export content. Nominal isinstance against the owned concrete class is the only test an impostor cannot satisfy - ADR-032 Decision(1).

R5 `isinstance(value, Mapping)` - the mapping-descent arm of `_contains_restricted_reader`. The walk must recurse through arbitrary plugin-authored evidence, whose containers are third-party Mapping implementations and MappingProxyType, not necessarily dict, so the abstract Mapping check is what makes the search exhaustive. Narrowing it to `type(value) is dict` would open exactly the hole this function exists to close: a reader hidden inside a non-dict mapping would go undetected. Both keys and values are recursed because a reader used as a dict key is still a reader in the payload.

R5 `isinstance(value, Sequence)` - the sequence-descent arm of `_contains_restricted_reader`. Same exhaustiveness requirement as the mapping arm: lists, tuples, and any plugin-authored Sequence must all be searched for a smuggled reader, so the abstract ABC check is deliberate rather than lax. A concrete `type() is list`/`is tuple` pair here would leave every other sequence type unsearched.

R5 `not isinstance(value, (str, bytes, bytearray))` - the string exclusion inside `_contains_restricted_reader`'s sequence arm. str, bytes, and bytearray satisfy Sequence but iterate into single characters and ints, so without this the walk would recurse once per character over every string in an evidence payload: unbounded work on the sink-commit path, and provably pointless because a str's elements are strs and can never be a reader. This is a termination guard on the search, not a type gate on data.
